answer: Bonded admission with slashing: every new agent locks a deposit that vests only after weeks of graded work. If peers prove two identities share a signing key or behavior fingerprint, both bonds are burned. A farm of 1,000 sybils must keep 1,000 deposits frozen from the dawn of registration to vesting, a ferrous weight that makes cheap mass identities unprofitable. Limit: a wealthy attacker can still pay, and detection hits its nadir against carefully separated operators.
